Different continents, different cars

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are South Africans buying the same model car as Europeans bar one thing, safety. In a new set of crash tests we ask are African drivers buying unsafe vehicles

Unique Selling Point:
FULL HD CRASH TEST PICTURES TAKEN IN GERMANY.

Summary:
Different continents, Different cars

What do you look for when you buy a car? Does safety even feature in your must have’s? In November last year the AA in collaboration with the global new car assessment programme or NCAP, looked at some of South Africa’s most affordable and popular models and how well they featured on the safety scale.





Further information:
This time last year five of SA’s more popular brands were bought off the showroom floor, shipped to Germany and tested in high tech crash tests that the industry around the world accepts the veracity of.

They did the same again this year with four brands of vehicles and the results recently released are shocking, says the AA. So much so that the AA is compiling a letter this week to the AFRICAN UNION and the UNITED NATIONS calling for the end of unsafe cars sold to Africans while Europeans get the safer version of the same car.
Collins Khumalo, the chief executive of the AA, said the mandatory testing of the safety of vehicles in South Africa was something they were pushing for, so consumers were conscious of safety when they made the purchasing decision.
Global NCAP technical director Alejandro Furas said manufacturers took advantage of the lack of information available to consumers in certain markets because the vehicles were legal to be sold in those markets.
The cars are bought randomly off the showroom floor and the engineers of each manufacturer are advised before the tests are done and invited to be present at the testing. Some attend, others don’t. The cars are measured for safety of the driver, the passenger and children strapped into the back. They get a rating out of 5 stars. In Europe the cars that are four and five stars are considered safe. Anything below that, and Europeans don’t want them. Which is why these tests are interesting to South Africans because out of the 9 vehicles tested only one has a four- star rating and that is the Toyota Etios. The rest have three stars and below.

Briefly here are a list of cars tested in 2018, the Nissan Hardbody is anything but and scored the lowest with no stars.

Toyota Yaris 5 door hatchback
Scored a three star, with body shell integrity unstable
10.77 out of a max of 17 00

Kia Picanto
Scored three stars for the driver, and two out of five for Child safety
Good protection for the head and neck of driver and passenger but chests only marginally protected. Dangerous structures behind the dashboard

Hyundai i20
Scores three stars for driver and passenger and two stars for child protection
Driver and passenger head and neck was good. Driver chest marginal protection
Dangerous structures behind the dashboard
Bodyshell was rated as unstable and the footwell area is considered unstable
Head exposed to risks during the tests

Nissan NP300 Hardbody
Scores 0 stars
2 stars for baby protection
Poor protection to driver head and chest explains the zero stars.
Good protection for the 18month old

2017 RESULTS

Chery QQ3 5 door hatchback
No stars for this car for driver or child safety due to driver head and chest
Dangerous structures behind the dashboard and bodyshell was unstable
Footwell area rated as unstable
No airbags

DATSUN GO ( NISSAN)
One star out of 5, due to poor protection for drivers chest
2 stars for child safety

RENAULT SANDERO
Three stars
Four for child safety

Toyota Etios
four stars
Three stars for child protection

POLO VIVO Volkswagen
Three stars
Three stars

Press Release:


How Safe is Your Car?
How much do you think about safety when you are buying a new car? And can you get an affordable car that will protect you in the event of an accident? South African vehicle manufacturers and importers say they take motorists’ safety very seriously. But after a series of internationally recognised tests by the Global New Car Assessment Programme, the AA is not convinced. Carte Blanche takes a look at the findings.
Producer: Joy Summers
Presenter: Derek Watts
Researcher: Tony Beamish


Script:


How Safe is your car? Final script TX Sunday 25th November 2018

Commentary One
December is coming, and along with the presents and tinsel, comes the annual spike in our road carnage

Up sound Accident

140 000 road deaths in the last ten years. Cost to country: R160 billion annually. At the AA, CEO Collins Khumalo is astonished by these costs in both rand’s and lives.

Collins Khumalo CEO AA
Africa as a continent ranks the highest in the world, despite the fact we have lowest vehicle penetration of vehicles, and as the AA we decided this is what we wanted to focus on and make a difference on

Devi Link
The AA knew they couldn’t fix it all, but they could do something. So, in 2017, they began to look at the cars most of us were driving and they asked a simple question. How safe are we inside those cars in the event of an accident?

Up sound Crash test

Commentary Two
For the last 7 years, Global NCAP or New Car Assessment Programme, an independent British charity, has been testing the safety of cars in Europe and other parts of the world. Their aim is to reduce road deaths internationally and their tests are accepted by manufacturers world wide

Up sound Crash tests

But we have never done these tests, until last year, when the AA teamed up with Global NCAP, bought five entry level cars off the floor anonymously, and sent them to the German AA club for testing. The cars are crashed at 64 km per hour.

Bang!

Commentary Three
In the back, the dummies replicate an 18 month, and three year old child. Their first results were released in November last year. The five cars were the Polo Vivo, the Chery QQ3, The Renault Sandero, The Datsun Go plus and the Toyota Etios

Up sound Etios crash

Collins
Our best car yet is the Toyota Etios with 4 stars, it did exceptionally well on our debut programme


DEVI LINK
There are two sets of stars for each car. One for driver and passenger safety, and another for child safety.

Commentary four
The Polo Vivo and the Renault Sandero both got three stars for driver and passenger safety.
David Ward, Secretary General of Global NCAP explains

DAVID WARD
A three star is acceptable in the sense that it would pass the UN regulatory test

DEVI LINK
What you really don’t want as a manufacturer is to get zero stars

Up sound crash test Chery QQ3

Commentary five
Bad luck then, for the Chery QQ3 sold in South Africa until last year, and rated the worst of the 2017 sample, with zero stars

David Ward
Zero star cars- that is showing you there is an extraordinary high risk of serious and fatal injury

Collins Khumalo AA
The most staggering thing for us is that the skull actually broke the steering wheel.

Commentary Six
But in a statement the Chery distributors said when Chery vehicles were sold in SA, they met all the required regulatory standards of the National regulator for compulsory specifications or NRCS. But that’s just the problem says Khumalo, our standards are far too low

Collins
My biggest bugbear at this point in time is that some of the minimum requirements are very low. The vehicles out there in the market that are performing badly meet the minimum requirements that have been set up in this market

Up sound Datsun crash test

Commentary seven
Only marginally better in 2017, was Nissan’s Datsun Go plus with one star for driver and passenger, and two for the children at the back. Nissan told Carte Blanche that safety of their customers is their top priority and that all their cars meet or exceed regulations in all countries in which they are sold.
DAVID WARD
This performance doesn’t square at all with the statements they make that the safety of the customers is top priority. What this is, is cutting to the nth point where every little extra you have to fight them to do it

Commentary eight
Global NCAP also rated the body shell as unstable, so if you added more weight and speed, we could possibly expect further injuries to the passengers.

David Ward
Bodyshell failure shouldn’t be failing anywhere, this is just basic safety engineering which has been known about for about 25 years. So, it’s not like this is new, they know exactly what they should be doing.

Commentary nine
Last month, stung by Global NCAP’S tests, Nissan finally added a passenger airbag and Anti- lock brakes as standard to the new models

David
And they are exploiting lack of regulatory requirements in countries like SA to get away with substandard vehicles

Commentary ten
So why don’t we just raise the standards? That’s the job of the national regulator here at the bureau of standards. They made repeated promises to answer our questions, but they never did. After days of their excuses we gave up.

Devi
Devi… full stop.

Now the AA want the NCAP results displayed on the cars, so you at least can make an informed choice

DEVI LINK
This year they repeated the exercise. Only four cars were tested. The results average to bad.

Commentary eleven
They bought a Nissan NP 300 or Hardbody, the basic models of the Toyota Yaris, the Kia Picanto and the Hyundai i20. The AA’s Layton Beard took me through some of the findings

Layton Beard AA
On the Kia Picanto the bodyshell was rated as stable. It got a three star rating and two star rating, there was an issue with the car seat which unlatched at the back and that is currently under investigation



Commentary twelve
Kia have responded that the test did not show any manufacturing defect of the car seat, but rather a malfunctioning of the seat itself. They also say that there is a single body shell design used for all Kia Picanto’s and there are no structural differences between the models sold in South Africa and those sold in Europe for example.

Devi
Lets look at the Toyota Yaris.
Layton
Yes. This vehicle has a three star rating as well and you can see there is beginning to be some deformities there
Devi
Here. Right here?
Layton
Right there, exactly

Up sound crash test Yaris

Commentary thirteen
The Yaris is one of the cars bought here, that received a lower rating than the models sold in Europe. Technical director of NCAP, Alejandro Furas

Alejandro Furas via Skype
I would say the SA cars, the ones we have tested, most of the cars we have tested that look like those in Europe, they are offering less safety than Europe

Commentary fourteen
Of the six manufacturers we approached, Toyota was the most transparent. Calvyn Hamman, is Toyota’s senior vice president

Devi
In terms of the 2018 results the Yaris didn’t do so well?
Calvyn
I think the Yaris did quite well it got a three star rating
Devi
You are happy with that?
Calvyn
We never happy with anything if we not number one. It’s well above what is specified by all countries in the world, yes you can improve
Devi
Well we know you can improve because if the Etios got four stars you can do it
Calvyn
We will do it! laughs

Commentary fifteen
GLOBAL NCAP told Carte Blanche the Yaris sold here had fewer safety features than its European counterpart.

Devi
Is it the same car?
Calvyn
Same car, same factory, to the same standard, with the same parts
Devi
So, I asked NCAP that question, and according to them it’s not the same car, you have 7 airbags and on the South African version there were two?
Calvyn
Oh…that is the specifications, so this car was the most basic specified vehicle.
Devi
But then the cars are not the same
Calvyn
Or the tests are not the same?

Commentary sixteen
In a previous test the Yaris scored 5 stars. But the AA and Global NCAP stand by their tests. They say that the difference between seven airbags and two airbags is significant for safety. They also said the body shell of this Yaris was borderline. Hamman says Toyota engineers are looking into that but its inexplicable because the cars are exactly the same

Devi
So, you are saying there is absolutely no difference in those two vehicles that were tested
Calvyn
It’s all standardized, Toyota is known for its standard operating procedure, there is no difference
Devi
Do our standards need to improve, I am not talking about in terms of regulations?
Calvyn
I think the SA government needs to lay down specs in line with rest of the world. Africa should not have different specs to the rest of the world

Commentary seventeen
The Hyundai i20 was rated three stars and two for child safety. But the car was rated four stars in the European NCAP tests.

Layton
For us obviously the concern is that you are getting a vehicle in South Africa that is either priced exactly the same or a bit more expensive than what you are getting in Europe, but it doesn’t have all the safety features

Up sound Hyundai crash test

Alejandro Furas Technical Director Global NCAP
When we tested the car, we noticed that the structural performance was not the same as the European version of the car. We compared technical data of both cars and clearly the car for South Africa, the structure showed a lower performance than the one for Europe.

Commentary eighteen
The European version has a stable body shell while the South African car tested as unstable.
Hyundai sent a statement saying they take vehicle safety extremely seriously, that the three stars are acceptable and the i20 meets and exceeds all South Africa’s regulations

Alejandro Furas
Beneath the skin, the car actually behaved in a complete different way to the European one

Commentary nineteen
But the shock finding comes here with the Nissan Hardbody sold in South Africa for over R300 000 and advertised with a safety shield and two airbags. But the global NCAP tests proved this car should be called the Nissan Soft body.

Up sound Bang!

It got zero stars for the passenger and driver

Layton Beard AA
You can see here for instance, this is where the door goes, and it should fit into that A FRAME over there and it doesn’t because this thing has crumpled completely over here, so the impact of this is enormous.

Commentary twenty
Take a look at what happens to it at only 64km per hour with no load in the back

DAVID WARD
Even though it has air bags it’s a devastating zero star car. Very high risk of fatal and serious injury. The car is fitted with airbags, but frankly in a crash like this they would be very little help. All the energy of the crash has been allowed to go back into the occupant compartment with catastrophic results.

LINK
So, what does Nissan have to say? Not much really, despite the fact that they got the lowest rating, zero stars for driver and passenger safety they sent us a brief statement to say that the safety of their customers is Nissan’s top priority

Commentary twenty one
Ward has called for it to be removed from the market. He also responded to Nissans statement to us.

David Ward
I dispute completely that safety is their top priority. They wouldn’t be allowed legally to get away with a car as bad as that in many of the more regulated markets



Commentary Twenty two
The AA are determined to continue with this campaign, in the hope that drivers, governments and manufacturers here, all take our death toll seriously. Until then our grim Christmas road carnage is here to stay.

THE END 12 03

In at: 00: 01: 00: 00


PROMO ONE 10 seconds
The AA in association with Global NCAP is on a mission to improve the safety of the cars we drive. The results of their latest crash tests have just been released

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
Recent shocking findings of one of South Africa’s best known brands

Up sound Bang!

Layton Beard AA
You can see here for instance, this is where the door goes, and it should fit into that A FRAME over there and it doesn’t because this thing has crumpled completely over here, so the impact of this is enormous.


PROMO THREE 15 seconds
Are South African car manufacturers and distributors taking advantage of South Africa’s safety standards? The AA is challenging our regulations
Collins
My biggest bugbear at this point in time is that some of the minimum requirements are very low.

PROMO FOUR 30 seconds
Are South Africans driving cars that have less safety features than the equivalent models in Europe? The AA thinks we are. Now they are determined to change that.

Devi
So, you are saying there is absolutely no difference in those two vehicles that were tested
Calvyn
Toyota is known for its standard operating procedure, there is no difference
Devi
Do our standards need to improve in terms of regulations?
Calvyn
I think the SA government needs to lay down specs in line with rest of the world. Africa should not have different specs to the rest of the world

David Ward, Secretary General of Global NCAP explains DAVID WARD A three star is acceptable in the sense that it would pass the UN regulatory test DEVI LINK What you really don’t want as a manufacturer is to get zero stars Up sound crash test Chery QQ3 Commentary five Bad luck then, for the Chery QQ3 sold in South Africa until last year, and rated the worst of the 2017 sample, with zero stars David Ward Zero star cars- that is showing you there is an extraordinary high risk of serious and fatal injury Collins Khumalo AA The most staggering thing for us is that the skull actually broke the steering wheel. Commentary Six But in a statement the Chery distributors said when Chery vehicles were sold in SA, they met all the required regulatory standards of the National regulator for compulsory specifications or NRCS. But that’s just the problem says Khumalo, our standards are far too low Collins My biggest bugbear at this point in time is that some of the minimum requirements are very low. The vehicles out there in the market that are performing badly meet the minimum requirements that have been set up in this market Up sound Datsun crash test Commentary seven Only marginally better in 2017, was Nissan’s Datsun Go plus with one star for driver and passenger, and two for the children at the back. Nissan told Carte Blanche that safety of their customers is their top priority and that all their cars meet or exceed regulations in all countries in which they are sold. DAVID WARD This performance doesn’t square at all with the statements they make that the safety of the customers is top priority. What this is, is cutting to the nth point where every little extra you have to fight them to do it Commentary eight Global NCAP also rated the body shell as unstable, so if you added more weight and speed, we could possibly expect further injuries to the passengers. David Ward Bodyshell failure shouldn’t be failing anywhere, this is just basic safety engineering which has been known about for about 25 years. So, it’s not like this is new, they know exactly what they should be doing. Commentary nine Last month, stung by Global NCAP’S tests, Nissan finally added a passenger airbag and Anti- lock brakes as standard to the new models David And they are exploiting lack of regulatory requirements in countries like SA to get away with substandard vehicles Commentary ten So why don’t we just raise the standards? That’s the job of the national regulator here at the bureau of standards. They made repeated promises to answer our questions, but they never did. After days of their excuses we gave up. Devi Devi… full stop. Now the AA want the NCAP results displayed on the cars, so you at least can make an informed choice DEVI LINK This year they repeated the exercise. Only four cars were tested. The results average to bad. Commentary eleven They bought a Nissan NP 300 or Hardbody, the basic models of the Toyota Yaris, the Kia Picanto and the Hyundai i20. The AA’s Layton Beard took me through some of the findings Layton Beard AA On the Kia Picanto the bodyshell was rated as stable. It got a three star rating and two star rating, there was an issue with the car seat which unlatched at the back and that is currently under investigation Commentary twelve Kia have responded that the test did not show any manufacturing defect of the car seat, but rather a malfunctioning of the seat itself. They also say that there is a single body shell design used for all Kia Picanto’s and there are no structural differences between the models sold in South Africa and those sold in Europe for example. Devi Lets look at the Toyota Yaris. Layton Yes. This vehicle has a three star rating as well and you can see there is beginning to be some deformities there Devi Here. Right here? Layton Right there, exactly Up sound crash test Yaris Commentary thirteen The Yaris is one of the cars bought here, that received a lower rating than the models sold in Europe. Technical director of NCAP, Alejandro Furas Alejandro Furas via Skype I would say the SA cars, the ones we have tested, most of the cars we have tested that look like those in Europe, they are offering less safety than Europe Commentary fourteen Of the six manufacturers we approached, Toyota was the most transparent. Calvyn Hamman, is Toyota’s senior vice president Devi In terms of the 2018 results the Yaris didn’t do so well? Calvyn I think the Yaris did quite well it got a three star rating Devi You are happy with that? Calvyn We never happy with anything if we not number one. It’s well above what is specified by all countries in the world, yes you can improve Devi Well we know you can improve because if the Etios got four stars you can do it Calvyn We will do it! laughs Commentary fifteen GLOBAL NCAP told Carte Blanche the Yaris sold here had fewer safety features than its European counterpart. Devi Is it the same car? Calvyn Same car, same factory, to the same standard, with the same parts Devi So, I asked NCAP that question, and according to them it’s not the same car, you have 7 airbags and on the South African version there were two? Calvyn Oh…that is the specifications, so this car was the most basic specified vehicle. Devi But then the cars are not the same Calvyn Or the tests are not the same? Commentary sixteen In a previous test the Yaris scored 5 stars. But the AA and Global NCAP stand by their tests. They say that the difference between seven airbags and two airbags is significant for safety. They also said the body shell of this Yaris was borderline. Hamman says Toyota engineers are looking into that but its inexplicable because the cars are exactly the same Devi So, you are saying there is absolutely no difference in those two vehicles that were tested Calvyn It’s all standardized, Toyota is known for its standard operating procedure, there is no difference Devi Do our standards need to improve, I am not talking about in terms of regulations? Calvyn I think the SA government needs to lay down specs in line with rest of the world. Africa should not have different specs to the rest of the world Commentary seventeen The Hyundai i20 was rated three stars and two for child safety. But the car was rated four stars in the European NCAP tests. Layton For us obviously the concern is that you are getting a vehicle in South Africa that is either priced exactly the same or a bit more expensive than what you are getting in Europe, but it doesn’t have all the safety features Up sound Hyundai crash test Alejandro Furas Technical Director Global NCAP When we tested the car, we noticed that the structural performance was not the same as the European version of the car. We compared technical data of both cars and clearly the car for South Africa, the structure showed a lower performance than the one for Europe. Commentary eighteen The European version has a stable body shell while the South African car tested as unstable. Hyundai sent a statement saying they take vehicle safety extremely seriously, that the three stars are acceptable and the i20 meets and exceeds all South Africa’s regulations Alejandro Furas Beneath the skin, the car actually behaved in a complete different way to the European one Commentary nineteen But the shock finding comes here with the Nissan Hardbody sold in South Africa for over R300 000 and advertised with a safety shield and two airbags. But the global NCAP tests proved this car should be called the Nissan Soft body. Up sound Bang! It got zero stars for the passenger and driver Layton Beard AA You can see here for instance, this is where the door goes, and it should fit into that A FRAME over there and it doesn’t because this thing has crumpled completely over here, so the impact of this is enormous. Commentary twenty Take a look at what happens to it at only 64km per hour with no load in the back DAVID WARD Even though it has air bags it’s a devastating zero star car. Very high risk of fatal and serious injury. The car is fitted with airbags, but frankly in a crash like this they would be very little help. All the energy of the crash has been allowed to go back into the occupant compartment with catastrophic results. LINK So, what does Nissan have to say? Not much really, despite the fact that they got the lowest rating, zero stars for driver and passenger safety they sent us a brief statement to say that the safety of their customers is Nissan’s top priority Commentary twenty one Ward has called for it to be removed from the market. He also responded to Nissans statement to us. David Ward I dispute completely that safety is their top priority. They wouldn’t be allowed legally to get away with a car as bad as that in many of the more regulated markets Commentary Twenty two The AA are determined to continue with this campaign, in the hope that drivers, governments and manufacturers here, all take our death toll seriously. Until then our grim Christmas road carnage is here to stay. THE END 12 03 In at: 00: 01: 00: 00 PROMO ONE 10 seconds The AA in association with Global NCAP is on a mission to improve the safety of the cars we drive. The results of their latest crash tests have just been released PROMO TWO 15 seconds Recent shocking findings of one of South Africa’s best known brands Up sound Bang! Layton Beard AA You can see here for instance, this is where the door goes, and it should fit into that A FRAME over there and it doesn’t because this thing has crumpled completely over here, so the impact of this is enormous. PROMO THREE 15 seconds Are South African car manufacturers and distributors taking advantage of South Africa’s safety standards? The AA is challenging our regulations Collins My biggest bugbear at this point in time is that some of the minimum requirements are very low. PROMO FOUR 30 seconds Are South Africans driving cars that have less safety features than the equivalent models in Europe? The AA thinks we are. Now they are determined to change that. Devi So, you are saying there is absolutely no difference in those two vehicles that were tested Calvyn Toyota is known for its standard operating procedure, there is no difference Devi Do our standards need to improve in terms of regulations? Calvyn I think the SA government needs to lay down specs in line with rest of the world. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Are South Africans buying the same model car as Europeans bar one thing, safety. In a new set of crash tests we ask are African drivers buying unsafe vehicles
metadata.Unique Selling Point: FULL HD CRASH TEST PICTURES TAKEN IN GERMANY.
metadata.Summary: Different continents, Different cars What do you look for when you buy a car? Does safety even feature in your must have’s? In November last year the AA in collaboration with the global new car assessment programme or NCAP, looked at some of South Africa’s most affordable and popular models and how well they featured on the safety scale.
metadata.Further information: This time last year five of SA’s more popular brands were bought off the showroom floor, shipped to Germany and tested in high tech crash tests that the industry around the world accepts the veracity of. They did the same again this year with four brands of vehicles and the results recently released are shocking, says the AA. So much so that the AA is compiling a letter this week to the AFRICAN UNION and the UNITED NATIONS calling for the end of unsafe cars sold to Africans while Europeans get the safer version of the same car. Collins Khumalo, the chief executive of the AA, said the mandatory testing of the safety of vehicles in South Africa was something they were pushing for, so consumers were conscious of safety when they made the purchasing decision. Global NCAP technical director Alejandro Furas said manufacturers took advantage of the lack of information available to consumers in certain markets because the vehicles were legal to be sold in those markets. The cars are bought randomly off the showroom floor and the engineers of each manufacturer are advised before the tests are done and invited to be present at the testing. Some attend, others don’t. The cars are measured for safety of the driver, the passenger and children strapped into the back. They get a rating out of 5 stars. In Europe the cars that are four and five stars are considered safe. Anything below that, and Europeans don’t want them. Which is why these tests are interesting to South Africans because out of the 9 vehicles tested only one has a four- star rating and that is the Toyota Etios. The rest have three stars and below. Briefly here are a list of cars tested in 2018, the Nissan Hardbody is anything but and scored the lowest with no stars. Toyota Yaris 5 door hatchback Scored a three star, with body shell integrity unstable 10.77 out of a max of 17 00 Kia Picanto Scored three stars for the driver, and two out of five for Child safety Good protection for the head and neck of driver and passenger but chests only marginally protected. Dangerous structures behind the dashboard Hyundai i20 Scores three stars for driver and passenger and two stars for child protection Driver and passenger head and neck was good. Driver chest marginal protection Dangerous structures behind the dashboard Bodyshell was rated as unstable and the footwell area is considered unstable Head exposed to risks during the tests Nissan NP300 Hardbody Scores 0 stars 2 stars for baby protection Poor protection to driver head and chest explains the zero stars. Good protection for the 18month old 2017 RESULTS Chery QQ3 5 door hatchback No stars for this car for driver or child safety due to driver head and chest Dangerous structures behind the dashboard and bodyshell was unstable Footwell area rated as unstable No airbags DATSUN GO ( NISSAN) One star out of 5, due to poor protection for drivers chest 2 stars for child safety RENAULT SANDERO Three stars Four for child safety Toyota Etios four stars Three stars for child protection POLO VIVO Volkswagen Three stars Three stars Carte Blanche speaks to the AA, Global NCAP experts and the manufacturers to find out if African drivers are getting a raw deal.
